candidate_nodes.label: prop:mw_i_11_orbit_from_whittaker
candidate_nodes.proof: Using 1.10, the proof reduces to the case where W_n is nonzero for all sufficiently large n. It introduces the test function phi_n supported on G_n with value chi_n^{-1} there and uses the trace identity dim W_n = (mes G_n)^(-1) tr pi(phi_n). For large n, tr pi(phi_n) is computed via the local character expansion 1.8, and the Fourier transform of phi_n composed with exp is shown to vanish unless the variable lies in varpi^(-2n)Y plus the annihilator of varpi^n E; otherwise it contributes a constant multiple of mes(varpi^n E). Therefore nonvanishing of tr pi(phi_n) forces the existence of some nilpotent orbit O with nonzero coefficient c_O meeting that translate of varpi^(-2n)Y. Since nilpotent orbits are stable under scalar multiplication, this gives intersections of O with Y plus a shrinking neighborhood of 0 for arbitrarily large n, and because there are only finitely many nilpotent orbits, one such orbit must have Y in its closure.

proof_steps.step: Apply Lemma 1.10 to assume W_n != 0 for all sufficiently large n.
Define phi_n on G, supported on G_n, and use dim W_n = (mes G_n)^(-1) tr pi(phi_n).
Compute the Fourier transform of phi_n o exp and deduce that tr pi(phi_n) can be nonzero only if some orbit with c_O != 0 meets varpi^(-2n)Y plus the annihilator of varpi^n E.

Rescale by scalar stability of nilpotent orbits to obtain intersections with Y plus shrinking neighborhoods of 0, then use finiteness of nilpotent orbits to conclude Y lies in the closure of one orbit with nonzero coefficient.

candidate_nodes.statement: If the degenerate Whittaker space attached to Y is nonzero, then there exists a nilpotent orbit O in g that occurs with nonzero coefficient in the local character expansion of tr pi near the identity and whose closure contains Y.

candidate_nodes.label: lem:mw_i_12_dimension_coefficient
candidate_nodes.proof: The proof explicitly reuses the notation and calculations from 1.11. By the maximality hypothesis on O = G.Y, for large n the support window isolated in 1.11 only sees the orbit O among the orbits with nonzero coefficients, so dim W_n is written as c_O times the orbital integral of phi_n o exp over O, hence as c_O times mes(varpi^n E) times a quotient-measure integral on O identified with G/G(Y). The proof then uses that t normalizes G(Y) and translates the relevant subset by t^(-n); after identifying this translated set with a small exponential neighborhood, an element exp X in it must preserve the character chi_n on G_n. By 1.6(iii), this forces X to lie in varpi^n m', which localizes the orbital integral to a quotient-measure factor over a finite-level quotient. The final displayed lines compute the determinant of t on g/y by pairing eigenvalues and then use the chosen orbital-measure normalization together with the Jacobian of exp on varpi^n E to cancel the remaining factor, yielding dim W_n = c_O. Because those determinant and measure formulas are partly obscured by OCR, the exact cancellation is left as a bridge request rather than claimed as fully reconstructed.

proof_steps.step: Reuse the trace formula and support computation from 1.11; maximality of O implies that for large n only O contributes among orbits with nonzero coefficients near the relevant support window.
Identify O with G/G(Y), note that t normalizes G(Y), and translate the support condition by t^(-n) so that it can be compared with a small exponential neighborhood exp(varpi^c m').
If exp X lies in the translated subset, then equality of the characters for all Z in varpi^n E means exp X normalizes chi_n; by 1.6(iii), this is equivalent to X lying in varpi^n m'.
Substitute this description into the orbital integral to express dim W_n as c_O times mes(varpi^n E) times a quotient-measure factor on a finite-level quotient attached to G(Y).

Use the determinant computation for t on g/y and the normalization of the exponential Jacobian to cancel the remaining factor and conclude dim W_n = c_O; the exact displayed cancellation is the unreconstructed step.

candidate_nodes.statement: Let O = G.Y and suppose its coefficient c_O in 1.8 is nonzero and Y does not lie in the closure of any other orbit with nonzero coefficient in 1.8. Then for all sufficiently large n, dim W_n is finite, independent of n, and equal to c_O.

payload.summary: Re-emitted the existing I.11 proposition and I.12 lemma with source-backed proof skeletons. Proposition I.11 is reconstructed through the finite-level trace formula, Fourier-support argument, and shrinking-neighborhood closure argument; Lemma I.12 is reconstructed through orbital-integral localization and the stabilizer criterion from 1.6(iii), with one bridge request isolating the OCR-damaged final determinant and measure-normalization cancellation.
